title: Module & Application Isolation
intro: Applies to: anything touching two modules, cross-module data, or two application surfaces (public app, admin panel, internal API). Isolation violations are the most expensive mistakes to unwind later; every MUST here is critical.

entries.rule: A module **MUST NOT** import another module's classes: no models, enums, events, commands, handlers, services, or value objects across bounded contexts.
allowed_in: pure infrastructure in the shared `Framework\` namespace
pure infrastructure in the shared `Shared\` namespace

checks.coverage: One layer per module, with no dependency allowed between module layers; the shared `Framework\` and `Shared\` namespaces are allowed from every layer. Covers imports and `::class` references, not class names in strings.

entries.rule: Cross-module collaboration **MUST** go through an explicit contract (interface) or a domain event, never direct imports or new-ing up another module's classes.
The consumer **MUST** define the contract; the provider implements it. An interface lives in the module that needs the capability, not the one that fulfills it.

There is no shared kernel for domain concepts: a module **MUST** own its own copy of any value object it needs rather than importing another module's. Only a dedicated shared-infrastructure namespace (`Framework\`, `Shared\`) holding pure infrastructure **MAY** be used from anywhere.
allowed_in: pure infrastructure in the shared `Framework\` namespace
pure infrastructure in the shared `Shared\` namespace

entries.rule: Cross-module references **MUST** be plain unsigned integer/ULID columns, never Eloquent relationships (`belongsTo` another module's model) and never database foreign keys across modules.

checks.coverage: The related model in `belongsTo` is a dependency on another module's layer, so the module-layer rules catch it. Database foreign keys in migrations are not covered.

entries.rule: Modules own their tables. A module **MUST NOT** add columns to another module's tables; it creates its own table keyed by the other module's id.
Cross-module data access **MUST** be read-only, via an injected `ConnectionInterface` with id-based queries. A module **MUST NOT** insert, update, or delete rows in another module's tables.
Data another module owns but this module needs at runtime **MUST** be materialized: stored on this module's own table and kept in sync by an event listener, not fetched cross-module per request.

sections.heading: Application isolation
intro: Separate application surfaces (the customer-facing app and an admin panel, for example) are separate applications, even inside one repository.

entries.rule: Application namespaces **MUST NOT** import from each other, in either direction: no shared models, enums, events, commands, handlers, or contracts.

checks.coverage: One layer per application namespace, with no dependency allowed in either direction.

entries.rule: Each application **MUST** own its read models (read-only, pointing at the same tables), its write models (carrying finders, invariants, and state transitions for anything it mutates), and its enums.

Cross-application event subscriptions **MUST NOT** exist: an application's provider never registers a listener on another application's event, by `::class` or by string FQCN. There is no listener exception.

checks.coverage: Catches a provider that names another application's event by `::class`. A listener registered by string FQCN is not covered.

entries.rule: Every side effect of an application's action (history rows, audit rows, cache flushes, notification emails) **MUST** be handled by that application's own listeners. An application **MUST NOT** dispatch another application's domain events to reuse its cascades; it replicates the steps it actually needs with its own write models.
A handler **MUST NOT** be a pass-through whose body only dispatches an event with no preceding mutation; it does real work against a write model or it does not exist.

checks.coverage: A custom rule that fails on a handler whose `handle()` body only dispatches an event. The rule does not exist yet.

entries.rule: Each application **MUST** authenticate through its own guard; guards and role enums are never shared across applications.

entries.note: Classes inside the same module using each other freely; the boundary is the bounded context, not the namespace segment.
Importing pure infrastructure from the shared `Framework\`/`Shared\` namespace.
A reporting or read-only context adding a query slice, an event listener, or a scheduled projection; only write commands are out of place there.
